metadata.title: Atomic Decomposition by Basis Pursuit

nodes.name: Dictionary and Atoms
nodes.statement: A dictionary is a collection of parameterized waveforms $\mathcal{D} = (\phi_\gamma : \gamma \in \Gamma)$ called atoms; each $\phi_\gamma$ is a discrete-time signal of length $n$.
nodes.statement_clean: A dictionary is a parameterized collection of waveforms (atoms) used to decompose signals.

nodes.name: Dirac Dictionary
nodes.statement: The Dirac dictionary consists of waveforms $\phi_\gamma(t) = \mathbf{1}_{\{t=\gamma\}}$ for $\gamma \in \{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$; this is the standard orthogonal basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

nodes.name: Heaviside Dictionary
nodes.statement: The heaviside dictionary consists of step waveforms $\phi_\gamma(t) = \mathbf{1}_{\{t \ge \gamma\}}$ for $\gamma \in \{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$; every signal admits the representation $s = s_0\phi_0 + \sum_{\gamma=1}^{n-1}(s_\gamma - s_{\gamma-1})\phi_\gamma$.

nodes.name: Fourier Dictionary
nodes.statement: A Fourier dictionary is a collection of sinusoidal atoms $\phi_{(\omega,0)} = \cos(\omega t)$, $\phi_{(\omega,1)} = \sin(\omega t)$ indexed by frequency $\omega \in [0,2\pi)$ and phase type $\nu \in \{0,1\}$. An $\ell$-fold overcomplete version uses $\omega_k = 2\pi k/(\ell n)$.

nodes.name: Haar Wavelet Dictionary
nodes.statement: Translations and dilations of mother wavelet $\psi = \mathbf{1}_{(1/2,1]} - \mathbf{1}_{[0,1/2]}$ and father wavelet $\varphi = \mathbf{1}_{[0,1]}$, with atoms $\phi_{(a,b,1)} = \psi(a(t-b))\sqrt{a}$ and $\phi_{(a,b,0)} = \varphi(a(t-b))\sqrt{a}$, indexed by scale $a$, location $b$, and gender $\nu$.

nodes.name: Gabor Dictionary
nodes.statement: Time-frequency atoms $\phi_\gamma(t) = \exp\{-(t-\tau)^2/(\delta t)^2\} \cdot \cos(\omega(t-\tau)+\theta)$ indexed by $\gamma=(\omega,\tau,\theta,\delta t)$.

nodes.name: Wavelet Packet and Cosine Packet Dictionaries
nodes.statement: Discrete-time dictionaries of about $n\log_2(n)$ waveforms (Coifman-Meyer); wavelet packet dictionary contains standard wavelets and oscillating waveforms; cosine packet dictionary contains windowed sinusoids of various widths and locations.

nodes.name: Stationary Wavelet Dictionary
nodes.statement: Overcomplete wavelet dictionary obtained by sampling locations more finely; at level $j$ contains $n$ (rather than $2^j$) circulant shifts of the basic wavelet of width $\approx n/2^j$. Total size $O(n\log_2 n)$, invariant under circulant shift.

nodes.name: Analysis vs Synthesis
nodes.statement: Synthesis: build a signal by superposing atoms via $s = \Phi\alpha$ ($n \times p$ matrix). Analysis: associate coefficients via $\tilde{\alpha} = \Phi^T s$ ($p \times n$ matrix). In overcomplete case ($p \gg n$), these are distinct operations.

nodes.name: Soft Threshold Nonlinearity
nodes.statement: $\eta_\lambda(y) = \mathrm{sgn}(y) \cdot (|y| - \lambda)_+$; equivalently the scalar minimizer $\eta_\lambda(y) = \arg\min_\xi \tfrac{1}{2}(y-\xi)^2 + \lambda|\xi|$.

nodes.name: Total Variation
nodes.statement: For an object $s$ with heaviside decomposition $s = \sum_i \alpha_i H_{t_i}$ vanishing at boundaries, $TV(s) = \sum_i |\alpha_i|$.

nodes.name: Overcomplete Signal Representation
nodes.statement: Given dictionary $\Phi$ ($n \times p$, $p > n$) and signal $s \in \mathbb{R}^n$, find coefficient vector $\alpha$ such that $\Phi\alpha = s$. Solution is non-unique; goal is sparsity, superresolution, and speed.

nodes.name: Basis Pursuit (BP)
nodes.statement: $\min \|\alpha\|_1$ subject to $\Phi\alpha = s$. Find a representation with minimal $\ell_1$ norm of coefficients in an overcomplete dictionary.

nodes.name: Method of Frames (MOF) Optimization
nodes.statement: $\min \|\alpha\|_2$ subject to $\Phi\alpha = s$. The unique solution is the minimum-length solution $\alpha^\dagger = \Phi^\dagger s = \Phi^T(\Phi\Phi^T)^{-1} s$.

nodes.name: Standard-Form Linear Program
nodes.statement: $\min c^T x$ subject to $Ax = b$, $x \ge 0$, where $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$, $A$ is $n \times m$.

nodes.name: Dual Linear Program
nodes.statement: $\max b^T y$ subject to $A^T y + z = c$, $z \ge 0$. Dual of (6.1); $x$ is the primal variable, $y,z$ are dual variables.

nodes.name: Basis Pursuit Denoising (BPDN)
nodes.statement: $\min_\alpha \tfrac{1}{2}\|y - \Phi\alpha\|_2^2 + \lambda \|\alpha\|_1$. Adapts BP to noisy data $y = s + \sigma z$; trades quadratic misfit against $\ell_1$ norm.

nodes.name: Total Variation Denoising
nodes.statement: $\min_g \tfrac{1}{2}\|y - g\|_2^2 + \lambda \cdot TV(g)$. Denoise images by penalized least squares with total variation penalty.

nodes.name: Perturbed Linear Program
nodes.statement: $\min c^T x + \tfrac{1}{2}\|\gamma x\|^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}\|p\|^2$ subject to $Ax + \delta p = b$, $x \ge 0$. With $\delta=1$ this solves BPDN; with small $\gamma,\delta$ it regularizes standard LP.

nodes.name: Signal Decomposition
nodes.statement: $s = \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} \alpha_\gamma \phi_\gamma$ (exact) or $s = \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_{\gamma_i} \phi_{\gamma_i} + R^{(m)}$ (approximate with residual).

nodes.name: Pseudoinverse Frame Solution
nodes.statement: $\alpha^\dagger = \Phi^\dagger s = \Phi^T(\Phi\Phi^T)^{-1} s$.

nodes.name: BP-to-LP Translation
nodes.statement: BP (3.1) recasts as LP (3.2) via $m \Leftrightarrow 2p$, $A \Leftrightarrow (\Phi, -\Phi)$, $b \Leftrightarrow s$, $c \Leftrightarrow (1;1)$, $x \Leftrightarrow (u;v)$, $\alpha \Leftrightarrow u-v$.

nodes.name: BPDN Lambda Choice
nodes.statement: $\lambda_p = \sigma\sqrt{2\log(p)}$, where $p$ is dictionary cardinality and $\sigma$ the noise level (assuming $\|\phi_\gamma\|_2 = 1$).

nodes.name: Central Equation in Interior-Point Step
nodes.statement: $(ADA^T + \delta^2 I)\Delta y = r + AD(t - X^{-1}v)$, with $D = (X^{-1}Z + \gamma^2 I)^{-1}$, residuals $t,r,v$, and updates $\Delta x = D(A^T\Delta y + X^{-1}v - t)$, $\Delta z = X^{-1}(v - Z\Delta x)$.

nodes.name: Solutions of LP as Bases
nodes.statement: If $A$ is $n \times m$ with $m > n$ and an optimal LP solution exists, then a solution exists with at most $n$ nonzero entries; generically (nondegenerate case), exactly $n$ nonzeros, and the corresponding columns form a basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
conclusions: A solution exists with at most $n$ nonzero entries
In generic (nondegenerate) case, exactly $n$ nonzeros and these columns form a basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$

nodes.name: LP Optimality via Duality
nodes.statement: $(x,y,z)$ solves the LP (6.1) if and only if the primal infeasibility $\|b-Ax\|_2$, the dual infeasibility $\|c - z - A^T y\|_2$, and the duality gap $c^T x - b^T y$ are all zero.
conclusions: $(x,y,z)$ optimal $\iff$ primal infeasibility, dual infeasibility, and duality gap are all zero

nodes.name: Soft Thresholding Equals BPDN in Orthogonal Basis
nodes.statement: When $\Phi$ is an orthogonal matrix and $\tilde{y} = \Phi^T y$, the BPDN solution coincides with coordinatewise soft thresholding $\hat{\alpha}_\gamma = \eta_\lambda(\tilde{y}_\gamma)$.

nodes.name: Ideal Atomic Decomposition (Donoho-Huo)
nodes.statement: For combined dictionary of sinusoids and Diracs, if signal $y$ is a superposition of fewer than $\sqrt{n}/2$ sinusoids and Diracs, then (a) the representation is unique, and (b) BP recovers it exactly.
assumptions: Combined dictionary of sinusoids and Diracs
Signal $y$ a superposition of $< \sqrt{n}/2$ sinusoids and Diracs
conclusions: BP recovers it exactly (frequencies, spike locations, amplitudes, signs)

nodes.name: Tight-Frame Closed-Form MOF
nodes.statement: For tight frame dictionaries (e.g. standard wavelet packet), $\|\Phi^T v\|_2 = L_n \cdot \|v\|_2$ with $L_n = \log_2(n)$, hence $\Phi^\dagger = L_n^{-1} \Phi^T$.
assumptions: Standard wavelet packet dictionary as instance

nodes.name: Method of Frames (MOF)
nodes.statement: Compute the minimum-$\ell_2$-norm solution of $\Phi\alpha = s$ via the generalized inverse $\alpha^\dagger = \Phi^T(\Phi\Phi^T)^{-1} s$.

nodes.name: Matching Pursuit (MP)
nodes.statement: Greedy algorithm: at each stage pick the dictionary atom most correlated with the current residual and add a scalar multiple to the approximation.
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize $s^{(0)}=0$, $R^{(0)}=s$. For $k=1,\ldots,m$: pick $\gamma_k = \arg\max_\gamma |\langle R^{(k-1)}, \phi_\gamma\rangle|$; set $\alpha_k = \langle R^{(k-1)}, \phi_{\gamma_k}\rangle$; update $s^{(k)} = s^{(k-1)} + \alpha_k \phi_{\gamma_k}$, $R^{(k)} = s - s^{(k)}$.

nodes.name: Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP)
nodes.statement: Refinement of MP that, at each step $m$, solves the least-squares problem $\min_{(\alpha_i)} \|s - \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i \phi_{\gamma_i}\|_2$ over all selected atoms; residual is orthogonal to selected atoms.
output: Sparse representation orthogonalized over selected atoms
nodes.origin_citation: Pati, Rezaiifar, Krishnaprasad 1993; Davis, Mallat, Zhang 1994

nodes.name: Best Orthogonal Basis (BOB)
nodes.statement: For wavelet/cosine packet dictionaries, adaptively select an orthogonal basis $B \subset \mathcal{D}$ that minimizes an additive entropy $E(s[B]) = \sum_I e(s[B]_I)$.
input: Wavelet packet or cosine packet dictionary $\mathcal{D}$
output: Best orthogonal basis $B^* = \arg\min\{E(s[B]) : B \text{ ortho basis} \subset \mathcal{D}\}$

nodes.name: BP-Simplex
nodes.statement: Apply the simplex method to the LP equivalent of BP: starting from any linearly independent collection of $n$ atoms, iteratively swap atoms to improve the objective until optimality.

nodes.name: BP-Interior (Primal-Dual Log-Barrier)
nodes.statement: Interior-point method for BP: starts from MOF solution, iteratively sparsifies $\alpha^{(k)}$ while maintaining near-feasibility, terminating when primal/dual infeasibility and duality gap fall below tolerances.
output: Approximate optimal $(x,y,z)$ encoding the BP solution $\alpha = u - v$
nodes.pseudocode:
1. Set tolerances FeaTol, PDGapTol and regularization $\gamma,\delta$.
2. Initialize $x>0$, $y=0$, $z>0$, $\mu>0$.
3. Loop: compute residuals $t = c + \gamma^2 x - z - A^T y$, $r = b - Ax - \delta^2 y$, $v = \mu e - Zx$, $D = (X^{-1}Z + \gamma^2 I)^{-1}$; solve $(ADA^T + \delta^2 I)\Delta y = r + AD(t-X^{-1}v)$ for $\Delta y$; set $\Delta x = D(A^T\Delta y + X^{-1}v - t)$, $\Delta z = X^{-1}(v - Z\Delta x)$; compute step sizes $\rho_p = .99\max\{\rho: x+\rho\Delta x \ge 0\}$, $\rho_d = .99\max\{\rho: z+\rho\Delta z \ge 0\}$; update $x,y,z,\mu$.
4. Terminate when primal infeasibility, dual infeasibility, and duality gap are below tolerances.

nodes.name: BPDN-Interior
nodes.statement: Variant of BP-Interior with regularization $\delta = 1$, applied to the perturbed LP equivalent of BPDN; fast implicit $\Phi, \Phi^T$ used in conjugate-gradient solves.

nodes.name: Block Coordinate Relaxation (BCR) for BPDN
nodes.statement: Minimize the BPDN objective by exploiting closed-form orthogonal-basis updates when $\Phi$ is a union of orthonormal complete matrices $\Phi^{(1)}, \ldots, \Phi^{(M)}$.
input: Dictionary as union of ortho matrices $\Phi^{(j)}$

nodes.name: Carbon
nodes.statement: Synthetic signal composed of six atoms (one Dirac, one sinusoid, four mutually orthogonal wavelet packet atoms). BP exactly recovers the six-atom decomposition; MOF is diffuse, MP makes mistakes on the four close atoms, BOB cannot resolve Dirac vs cosine nonorthogonality.

nodes.name: TwinSine
nodes.statement: Two cosines separated by less than the Rayleigh distance $2\pi/n$ analyzed in fourfold overcomplete discrete cosine dictionary. MOF gives broad oscillatory output, MP picks the in-between frequency and never recovers, BP correctly resolves the doublet (also in noisy case).

nodes.name: FM-Cosine
nodes.statement: Signal $s = \cos(\xi_0 t) + \cos((\xi_0 t + \alpha\cos(\xi_1 t))t)$ analyzed with cosine packet dictionary. BP cleanly separates the FM and pure-sine components; BOB and MP fail.

nodes.name: Gong
nodes.statement: Signal that vanishes until $t_0$ then follows a decaying sinusoid; analyzed in cosine packet dictionary. BP gives finest representation of decay structure; BPDN outperforms MOF/BOB/MP visually at SNR=1.

nodes.name: WernerSorrows
nodes.statement: Superposition of chirps, sinusoids, and Diracs. With Coifman-Wickerhauser entropy, BOB chooses a global sinusoid basis and misses chirp structure; using $\ell_1$ entropy with BOB improves; BP reveals structure best of all.

nodes.name: DeVore-Temlyakov MP Counterexample
nodes.statement: Dictionary of $n+1$ atoms: first $n$ Dirac atoms plus a final atom $\phi_{n+1}(t) = c$ for $1\le t\le 10$, $\phi_{n+1}(t) = c/(t-10)$ for $10 < t \le n$ (normalized). Signal $s_t = 10^{-1/2} \mathbf{1}_{\{1\le t\le 10\}}$ has exact $A=10$-atom decomposition, but greedy MP error decays only as $O(1/\sqrt{m})$.

nodes.name: Chen's OMP Counterexample
nodes.statement: With $A=10$, $n=1024$, dictionary $\phi_i = \delta_i$ for $1 \le i \le 10$ and $\phi_i = a s + \sqrt{1-a}\, e_i$ for $11 \le i \le n$ ($a = 2/10$), OMP picks all atoms with $\gamma > A$ before any of the first $A$, yielding $\|\bar{R}^{[m]}\|_2 = (1-a)/\sqrt{1+(m-1)a}$ rather than ideal zero error after $A$ steps.

nodes.name: HeaviSine with Stationary Wavelet Dictionary
nodes.statement: BP coefficients on signal HeaviSine in stationary symmlet-8 dictionary closely match the multiscale-edge representation: at fine scales there is virtually a one-to-one relationship between BP-selected wavelets and CWT maxima.

nodes.name: Blocks (Total Variation Denoising)
nodes.statement: Piecewise-constant signal Blocky has sparse representation in heavisides; BPDN with heaviside dictionary (= TV denoising) outperforms wavelet shrinkage and BPDN with jump+wave merger.

nodes.name: Cusp (Jump+Wave Dictionary)
nodes.statement: Piecewise-smooth signal Cusp lacks sparse heaviside representation; BPDN with merged jump+wave (tapered heavisides + S8-symmlet wavelets) avoids stairstep artifacts of TV denoising.

nodes.name: MOF Sparsity Failure
nodes.statement: MOF is not sparsity preserving: each atom with nonzero inner product with the signal is typically a member of the solution. MOF is also intrinsically resolution limited: reconstruction is $\Phi^\dagger \Phi \alpha$, spatially spread out.

nodes.name: MP Myopia
nodes.statement: Because MP is myopic, in non-orthogonal dictionaries it may choose wrongly in the first iterations and spend most of its time correcting these mistakes (illustrated by TwinSine, DeVore-Temlyakov, and Chen examples).

nodes.name: Fast Implicit Algorithms
nodes.statement: Only dictionaries with fast implicit algorithms for $\Phi\alpha$ and $\Phi^T s$ are considered: FFT for Fourier ($O(n\log n)$); Haar/S8-symmlet wavelets ($O(n)$); stationary wavelets, cosine packets, wavelet packets ($O(n\log n)$).

nodes.name: Conjugate-Gradient Substitute for Sparsity
nodes.statement: Standard interior-point LP codes exploit sparsity of $A$, but BP's $A$ is dense. Substitute: use fast implicit $\Phi,\Phi^T$ and conjugate-gradient methods (e.g. LSQR) to solve central equations $(ADA^T + \delta^2 I)v$ without forming $A$ explicitly.

nodes.name: BP-Interior Improves on MOF
nodes.statement: BP-interior initializes with the MOF solution and iteratively improves it; in this sense BP sequentially improves on MOF.

nodes.name: BOB-Initialization for BP-Simplex
nodes.statement: Natural initialization for BP-simplex: use the Coifman-Wickerhauser BOB as the starting basis. BP can then be viewed as refining BOB by swapping nonorthogonal atoms with orthogonal ones whenever this improves the objective.

nodes.name: Routine Settings for BP
nodes.statement: Recommended routine: primal-dual log-barrier with fast implicit $A,A^T$, FeaTol = PDGapTol = $10^{-1}$, CGAccuracy = $10^{-1}$. Use $10^{-2}$ or $10^{-3}$ for superresolution. Set $\delta = 10^{-4}$ for BP, $\delta = 1$ for BPDN.

nodes.name: Soft-thresholding scalar identity
nodes.statement: Recall $\eta_\lambda(y) = \arg\min_\xi \tfrac{1}{2}(y-\xi)^2 + \lambda|\xi|$, the scalar soft-threshold minimizer.

nodes.name: Rewrite BPDN in coefficient coordinates
nodes.statement: By orthogonality of $\Phi$, $\|y - \Phi\alpha\|_2 = \|\tilde{y} - \alpha\|_2$, so BPDN becomes $\min_\alpha \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_\gamma (\tilde{y}_\gamma - \alpha_\gamma)^2 + \lambda \sum_\gamma |\alpha_\gamma|$.

nodes.name: Apply scalar minimizer coordinatewise
nodes.statement: Apply (5.2) to each coordinate independently to obtain $\hat{\alpha}_\gamma = \eta_\lambda(\tilde{y}_\gamma)$, establishing the claim.

nodes.name: Set parameters
nodes.statement: Set feasibility tolerance FeaTol, duality-gap tolerance PDGapTol, and regularization parameters $\gamma, \delta$ (e.g. $10^{-4}$).

nodes.name: Initialize variables
nodes.statement: Initialize $x > 0$, $y = 0$, $z > 0$, $\mu > 0$.

nodes.name: Main interior-point loop
nodes.statement: Repeat: (a) compute residuals $t = c + \gamma^2 x - z - A^T y$, $r = b - Ax - \delta^2 y$, $v = \mu e - Zx$ and $D = (X^{-1}Z + \gamma^2 I)^{-1}$; (b) solve $(ADA^T + \delta^2 I)\Delta y = r + AD(t - X^{-1}v)$ via conjugate gradients, set $\Delta x = D(A^T\Delta y + X^{-1}v - t)$, $\Delta z = X^{-1}(v - Z\Delta x)$; (c) compute step sizes $\rho_p = .99\max\{\rho: x+\rho\Delta x \ge 0\}$, $\rho_d = .99\max\{\rho: z+\rho\Delta z \ge 0\}$ and update $x \leftarrow x+\rho_p\Delta x$, $y \leftarrow y+\rho_d \Delta y$, $z \leftarrow z+\rho_d\Delta z$, $\mu \leftarrow (1-\min(\rho_p,\rho_d,.99))\mu$.
